newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Jan inflation steady at 6.6 pct year on year.
newsitem.headline: HK Jan inflation steady at 6.6 pct year on year.

text.p: Hong Kong's consumer price index (A), the broadest measure of inflation, rose 6.6 percent year-on-year in January versus a 6.7 percent increase in December, the Census and Statistics Department said on Monday. Analysts noted the January inflation rate rose only slightly from the previous month but said bigger increases were expected later this year.
"It's a bit lower than expected," said Shamus Mok, chief economist at Bank of East Asia, adding that stable food prices could have helped to curb inflation last month.
"But that does not mean the February figure will also be so low," he said. "We should wait for a few more months before we can tell the trend."
Rising rents were expected to push up inflation this year, he said.
CPI (A) stood at a yearly 5.8 percent in January 1996.
